hero.subtitle: If a diagnostic error, surgical mistake, or medication mix-up at a Signal Hill area hospital or clinic left you injured, our team can review your case and help you understand your options under California's MICRA rules.

about.title: Signal Hill Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Signal Hill sits within Los Angeles County, and residents here typically rely on hospitals and outpatient clinics scattered across the greater Long Beach and LA medical corridor for everything from routine procedures to emergency care. When something goes wrong — a delayed diagnosis, a surgical error, an anesthesia mistake, or a medication mix-up — the aftermath can be confusing on top of being painful. California's MICRA law adds extra layers most people never anticipate: a short window to act, a mandatory 90-day notice before filing suit, and a requirement that a qualified medical expert review the case before it can move forward. We handle medical malpractice cases on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered on your behalf. Our team listens to what happened, asks the right questions, and reviews whether your situation may support a claim.
commonInjuries: Delayed or missed diagnosis of a serious condition

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Facts Matter Under California Law

items.title: The Clock Starts Early
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a malpractice claim. Waiting to sort things out can cost you the right to pursue a claim at all.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed, California law requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider. We make sure this step is handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Isn't Optional
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, California almost always requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on whether the care fell below an acceptable standard. Acting early gives more time to gather that kind of review.

items.question: I live in Signal Hill but was treated at a hospital outside the city — does that matter?
items.answer: Not really. Because Signal Hill is a small city within Los Angeles County, most residents are treated at facilities located elsewhere in the county, and that's fine. What matters is where the care happened and when, not your home address, and we can sort out the right jurisdiction.

items.question: How long do I actually have to bring a claim?
items.answer: Under MICRA, it's generally one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, with an outer limit of three years from the date of injury. There's also a required 90-day notice before filing suit, so acting sooner rather than later gives everyone more room to work.

items.question: Is there a cap on what I can recover?
items.answer: California law does place a cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in medical malpractice cases, though that cap is set to rise each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, generally aren't subject to that same cap. We can walk through how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: Is there a charge for a case review?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews at no cost. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a recovery.
